events.title: The conquest of Sri Lanka begins; Anuradhapura taken
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: Rajaraja takes Anuradhapura and moves the capital
events.evidence: The Chola inscriptions in Sri Lanka, the Mahavamsa's account, and the Shiva temples built at Polonnaruwa.
events.becomes: Polonnaruwa becomes the island's capital and stays so for three centuries after the Cholas leave; and a Tamil-speaking population is established in the north that is still there.

events.title: Atisha Dipankara leaves for Tibet
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.
events.note: Fifty years before Vikramashila was ash, and what he carried was not.

events.title: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu — Telugu literature begins
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Revenue classified by soil, water access and crop
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.

events.title: The Jewish copper plates of Bhaskara Ravi Varman
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Kamakhya temple tradition; Tantric transmission
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Kathasaritsagara's Kashmiri court patronage
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Manipravalam register: Sanskrit and Malayalam fused
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Bakhshali manuscript survives incomplete
events.evidence: The birch-bark leaves themselves, found in fragments in a field in 1881 and radiocarbon-dated across several centuries.

events.title: Inscriptions are chiselled out by successors
events.evidence: The erasures themselves, which usually leave enough to read what was removed.
events.note: The record's own record of being edited.

events.title: Insects and rodents take what damp does not
events.evidence: The precautions themselves: manuscript chests, neem leaves, turmeric and the recopying schedules that assume loss.

events.title: Nambi Andar Nambi recovers the Tevaram hymns
events.evidence: The Chola-period tradition of the recovery and the arrangement that followed it.

events.title: Chola inscriptions record dues from forest produce
events.evidence: Revenue categories in temple and village inscriptions covering honey, wax, timber and elephants.
events.note: The forest enters the ledger. The people are still not named.

events.title: The Kalika Purana is compiled in the valley
events.evidence: The text, whose ritual geography is specific to Kamakhya and the Brahmaputra.

events.title: The Pala illuminated palm-leaf manuscripts
events.evidence: The dated Ashtasahasrika Prajnaparamita manuscripts, many now in Nepal and Tibet.

events.title: The Jewish copper plates grant a merchant seventy-two privileges
events.evidence: The plates themselves, held at Kochi, granting rights to Joseph Rabban and his descendants.

events.title: Matrilineal inheritance becomes the region's dominant property system
events.evidence: The temple and household records of taravad property, and the colonial-era legal commissions that documented it.
events.note: Property and descent through the mother's line, for most of the population, for nine centuries.

events.title: The Kerala temple style: timber roofs, circular sanctums, and a monsoon to survive
events.evidence: The surviving temples and their carpentry, and the Tantrasamuchaya's building prescriptions.

events.title: Kumbakonam's temple cluster becomes a delta town of shrines
events.evidence: The Nageswaran and Sarangapani temples and their inscription series.

events.title: Abhinavagupta's Abhinavabharati preserves a Natyashastra now lost
events.evidence: The commentary, which quotes readings and whole earlier commentators that survive nowhere else.
events.note: We read the Natyashastra partly through a man who was reading a better copy.

events.title: Narayana's Hitopadesha reworks the Panchatantra
events.evidence: The text, which names its source, and the manuscript tradition from Bengal.

events.title: The Mayamata codifies the southern building canon
events.evidence: The text, and its correspondence with what the Chola temples actually do.

events.title: The Kerala and Pandya campaigns
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: Its inscriptions name 400 dancers, singers and staff — individually
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Brihadeeswarar temple at Thanjavur completed
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The temple as employer, landlord, bank and archive at once
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.

events.title: Rajendra I accedes
events.evidence: Inscriptions dated in regnal years, coinage, and the dynastic lists that later chronicles compile from both.

events.title: Ramanuja born; the Srivaishnava tradition takes shape
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Sri Lanka campaign completed; Polonnaruwa made capital
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: The Ganges expedition; Gangaikonda Cholapuram founded
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: Ganges water carried south in golden pots — sovereignty as ritual
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The naval expedition to Srivijaya
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.

events.title: The Chola fleet crosses the Bay and raids Srivijaya
events.evidence: The Tanjore inscription listing the ports taken, and the Chinese record of the embassies before and after.
events.becomes: The Bay of Bengal trade reorganises around Chola-protected routes; the Ayyavole guild operates from Java to the Gulf; and an embassy of seventy-two merchants reaches the Song court in 1077.
events.note: The only recorded transoceanic invasion launched from India. It was a trade dispute.

events.title: Gangaikonda Cholapuram is laid out as a capital, not just a temple
events.evidence: The temple, the six-kilometre Chola Gangam tank, and the palace mound at Maligaimedu.

events.title: Hoysala foundation
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Mahmud of Ghazni reaches Somnath
events.evidence: The Ghaznavid court histories, Al-Biruni who travelled with the campaigns, and the temple's rebuilding record.
events.becomes: Al-Biruni's Tarikh al-Hind, written because a scholar attached to the campaigns learned Sanskrit and read the sources; and, in the other direction, six centuries of argument about the raid that are still going on.

events.title: Embassies to Song China; the Quanzhou trade
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.

events.title: The Chola Gangam and the great delta tanks are cut
events.evidence: The surviving bund, and the inscriptions recording tank committees and desilting duties.

events.title: Al-Biruni finishes the Tarikh al-Hind
events.evidence: The Arabic text, which states its own date and its method: learn the language, read the sources, report the disagreements.
events.note: He learned Sanskrit to write it, and said outright where he thought his own sources were unreliable.

events.title: The Dilwara temples at Mount Abu
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Chola bronze casting at its height; the Nataraja form matures
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Chola-Chalukya wars grind over Vengi for a century
events.evidence: Both dynasties' inscription series, which claim the same victories.
events.becomes: Exhaustion on both sides, and a Chalukya prince on the Chola throne in 1070 — the war ends in a succession, not a conquest.

events.title: Bhoja's Samarangana Sutradhara: architecture, and machines
events.evidence: The text, with its chapters on town planning, temple form and yantra.

events.title: Gangaikondacholapuram temple completed
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Pala Buddhism transmits wholesale to Tibet
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.

events.title: The Kaveri floods across the delta
events.evidence: Inferred from repair endowments in temple inscriptions rather than from a flood record. Generated to stand for a class of event the inscriptions imply and do not date.

events.title: The Hoysala and Chalukya tank cascades are cut across the Deccan plateau
events.evidence: The surviving tank chains and the inscriptions recording their construction and maintenance committees.

events.title: Kshemendra writes satires on the professions of his own city
events.evidence: The Narmamala and Desopadesa, which name the clerk, the physician and the bawd and describe their frauds.

events.title: The Vetala Panchavimshati: twenty-five riddles told by a corpse
events.evidence: The versions embedded in the Kathasaritsagara and the Brihatkathamanjari.

events.title: The Ayyavole guild operates from Java to the Persian Gulf
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.

events.title: Rani ki Vav is built by a queen for her husband's memory
events.evidence: The stepwell itself, and the Prabandha tradition's attribution to Udayamati.

events.title: Kulottunga unites Chola and Eastern Chalukya lines
events.evidence: Inscriptions dated in regnal years, coinage, and the dynastic lists that later chronicles compile from both.

events.title: The Senas; brahmanical reordering
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Vijayabahu restores independence; Polonnaruwa
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: An embassy of seventy-two merchants reaches the Song court
events.evidence: Goods found far from where they were made, and the documents of the people who moved them.

events.title: The Eastern Gangas
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Kulottunga abolishes tolls — Sungam Tavirtta
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Kakatiya foundation
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Airavatesvara at Darasuram begun
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Chola wars exhaust the Cheras
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: Famine and flood in the valley, recorded year by year
events.evidence: Kalhana's chronicle, which gives the grain price and the mortality for successive years.

events.title: Kamarupa fragments; the Chutiya and Kachari rise
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Ramanuja at Srirangam; temple administration reformed
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Charyapada — the earliest Bengali (and Assamese, and Odia) verse
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Vijnaneshwara's Mitakshara — the standard commentary on Hindu law
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Sectarian disputes destroy rival institutions' records
events.evidence: Inscriptional erasures and re-dedications, which are physical and visible on temple walls.

events.title: The Nath siddhas cut across religion and caste and leave verse behind
events.evidence: The Gorakh bani, the Charyapada, and the Nath monastic network from Nepal to Gujarat.

events.title: The Lingaraj temple and the mature Kalinga building canon
events.evidence: The temple itself, and the Bhubaneswar sequence of some five hundred shrines from the seventh century onward.

events.title: The Chera Perumals end; Kerala fragments into chiefdoms
events.evidence: A convention. Eras are drawn by historians, not lived by anyone.

events.title: Temple entry disputes recorded in inscription
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Kalingattuparani; war poetry as court literature
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Ramanuja's Sribhasya answers Shankara
events.evidence: The text, and the Srirangam temple's inscriptions recording its teaching.

events.title: Basava and the Sharanas; the Anubhava Mantapa
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Basava and the Sharanas; vachana poetry by artisans and washerwomen
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Akka Mahadevi; a woman's voice at the centre of a movement
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Akka Mahadevi; vachanas by weavers, potters, washerwomen
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Hemachandra's Siddha-Hema: a grammar for six languages at once
events.evidence: The text, commissioned by Jayasimha Siddharaja and carried through Gujarat on an elephant.
events.note: A grammar given a public procession. Somebody thought language was worth a parade.

events.title: Kalhana's Rajatarangini
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Rajatarangini — the first Indian work that is recognisably history
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Belur and Halebidu; the Hoysala style
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Bhaskara II: Lilavati and Siddhanta Shiromani
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Hoysaleswara; the Hoysala style
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Jain bhandara libraries at Jaisalmer and Patan
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.
events.note: Much of what survives from western India survives because merchants paid to keep it dry.

events.title: Jain merchant capital funds libraries — the bhandaras
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.

events.title: Kamba Ramayanam — not a translation but a rival
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The great tanks begin to silt faster than they are dredged
events.evidence: Tank sediment profiles, and the rising frequency of desilting endowments in the inscriptions.

events.title: The Virashaivas reject temple, priest and caste in one movement
events.evidence: The vachana corpus and the Basava Purana.

events.title: The Kakatiya tank cascades irrigate an upland with no river
events.evidence: The Pakhal, Ramappa and Laknavaram tanks, and the inscriptions recording their construction and their maintenance committees.
events.note: Thousands of linked tanks on a plateau with no perennial river. Most are still in use.

events.title: The Jain bhandaras are organised as lending libraries with catalogues
events.evidence: The surviving catalogues, borrowing records, and the manuscripts themselves with their custody notes.
events.note: A library with a catalogue and a lending register, in the twelfth century, funded by merchants.

events.title: The Sharanas compose vachanas in spoken Kannada
events.evidence: The vachana corpus itself, signed with each author's ankita, and the trades its authors name as their own.
events.note: Written by washerwomen, cobblers, boatmen and ferrymen. Signed. In their own language.

events.title: The Sri Lankan tank system reaches its greatest extent
events.evidence: The tanks themselves, and the Culavamsa account of Parakramabahu's works.

events.title: The Jagannath temple at Puri completed
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The three nikayas are unified under the Mahavihara
events.evidence: Parakramabahu's Galvihara inscription, which sets out the terms of the reform.

events.title: Jayadeva's Gita Govinda
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The Kakatiyas and tank irrigation across the Telangana uplands
events.evidence: The building, and the inscription on it.

events.title: The Ghurids are beaten at Kasahrada before they win at Tarain
events.evidence: The Jain chronicles of Gujarat and the Persian accounts, which both record the defeat.
events.becomes: Muhammad of Ghor turns north instead, and the Punjab route becomes the one that matters. Gujarat buys itself another century and a half.
events.note: A defeat that redirected an invasion. The gate has more than one door.

events.title: The Yadavas of Devagiri
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Pandya resurgence; Chola territory contracts
events.evidence: Inscriptions dated in regnal years, coinage, and the dynastic lists that later chronicles compile from both.

events.title: The Hoysalas and Yadavas fight over the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
events.evidence: The inscription record of both dynasties across the contested districts.
events.becomes: Both are still fighting each other when Delhi arrives, and neither can answer it.

events.title: First Tarain — Prithviraj wins
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: Second Tarain: the hinge of the medieval period
events.evidence: The Persian chronicles, and the abrupt change in the epigraphic and numismatic record across the north.
events.becomes: The Delhi Sultanate; Persian as a court and literary language; Amir Khusrau, who wrote in it and in Hindavi both; the Indo-Islamic building tradition; and the arrival of paper, which cut the cost of a copy by an order of magnitude.

events.title: Nalanda sacked; Vikramashila and Odantapuri follow
events.evidence: Persian chronicles written for the victors; a destruction layer at the site; and the negative evidence of texts surviving only in Tibetan and Chinese.

events.title: Odantapuri is destroyed
events.evidence: Persian and Tibetan accounts; the site is poorly excavated and the date is inferred from the campaign sequence.

events.title: Calicut rises; the Zamorin and the pepper trade
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Kashmiri Sanskrit scholarship at its widest influence
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Ramappa temple; floating brick and sandbox foundations
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Jagannath cult absorbs tribal, Jain and Buddhist strands
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Kerala's manuscript tradition keeps recopying and most of it still goes
events.evidence: Surviving palm-leaf collections against the works their own colophons reference.

events.title: Somapura is abandoned
events.evidence: Burn layers and the end of occupation at Paharpur; the cause is not established.

events.title: Vikramashila is destroyed
events.evidence: Tibetan accounts of the flight of scholars, and the site's abrupt archaeological end.

events.title: The shifting cultivation cycle holds against the plough
events.evidence: Continuity of jhum in the hills against settled wet rice on the Brahmaputra plain, both attested throughout.
events.note: Two agricultures on either side of a line, neither replacing the other for a thousand years.

events.title: The Chishti khanqahs open their kitchens to whoever comes
events.evidence: The malfuzat literature, the Ajmer and Delhi dargah endowments, and the sama' controversy.

events.title: Kakatiya inscriptions record donors from outside the old landed families
events.evidence: The inscription corpus, in which nayaka and cultivator donors appear in numbers for the first time.

events.title: The Chutiya, Kachari and Koch kingdoms hold the valley's other quarters
events.evidence: The dynastic records, the Dimapur and Koch Behar remains, and the Ahom buranjis' accounts of them.

events.title: Harihara and Raghavanka break the Sanskrit metres for Kannada ones
events.evidence: The Girijakalyana and the Harishchandra Kavya, and the shatpadi metre they established.

events.title: The Guhilas at Chittor, and a fort that becomes a symbol
events.evidence: The Chittor inscriptions and the fort's building sequence.

events.title: Zinc is distilled at Zawar by downward condensation
events.evidence: The retort furnaces at Zawar, the slag heaps, and the metallurgical analysis of the residues.
events.note: Distilling zinc requires condensing a vapour below its boiling point. Europe managed it in 1738.

events.title: The Siddhar poets write medicine, alchemy and abuse of the priesthood
events.evidence: The Siddhar corpus, and the Siddha medical tradition's own textual lineage.

events.title: Warangal's concentric fort and its four gateways
events.evidence: The granite and earth ramparts and the four freestanding torana gateways still in place.

events.title: The Sukasaptati: seventy tales told by a parrot to delay a wife
events.evidence: The Sanskrit recensions, and the Persian Tutinama that derives from them.

events.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji takes Nadia and then Bengal
events.evidence: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, and the coin and inscription record of the new Bengal administration.
events.becomes: The Bengal Sultanate, which within a century was patronising Bengali rather than Persian — the first state anywhere to give the language a court.

events.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji's Tibet expedition destroyed in the hills
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: The Delhi Sultanate founded
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Jagaddala ends and its scholars go to Tibet
events.evidence: Tibetan colophons naming Jagaddala scholars arriving; the monastery itself was only located in the twentieth century.

events.title: Magha of Kalinga takes Polonnaruwa and the dry zone is abandoned
events.evidence: The Culavamsa's account, and the archaeological evidence for the abandonment of the tank civilisation.
events.note: The tanks silt up and the population moves southwest. A thousand years of hydraulic engineering ends in a generation.

events.title: The capital moves southwest, and keeps moving
events.evidence: The Dambadeniya, Yapahuwa, Kurunegala and Gampola sequence in the Culavamsa and the building record.

events.title: Genghis Khan reaches the Indus and turns back
events.evidence: Juzjani and Juvaini, and the Sultanate's own account of Jalal ad-Din's flight across the river.
events.becomes: A frontier policy: for eighty years the Sultanate's whole military effort goes into the northwest, which is why it takes so long to move south.

events.title: Sukaphaa crosses the Patkai — the Ahom kingdom begins
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Sharngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara, written at Devagiri
events.evidence: The text, which both the Hindustani and Carnatic traditions treat as the last common authority.
events.note: Written just before the traditions parted. Both still cite it.

events.title: Konark; the Sun Temple as a stone chariot
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The paik system: labour service as the basis of the state
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.
events.note: An army, a road corps and a public works department, all paid in land instead of money.

events.title: Madhva argues for difference against Shankara's identity
events.evidence: His commentaries and the Udupi matha tradition.

events.title: Rani Rudrama Devi rules in her own name
events.evidence: Inscriptions dated in regnal years, coinage, and the dynastic lists that later chronicles compile from both.

events.title: The Mahanubhava sect writes prose in Marathi and encrypts it
events.evidence: The Lilacharitra, and the sect's sakala cipher scripts.
events.note: They wrote their scripture in code to keep it from outsiders. It nearly worked too well.

events.title: The Lilacharitra: the first biography written in Marathi prose
events.evidence: The text, compiled from the recollections of Chakradhar's disciples and dated by internal evidence.

events.title: The last Chola. The focus period closes
events.evidence: A convention. Eras are drawn by historians, not lived by anyone.

events.title: Twipra (Manikya) in the Tripura hills
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Jnaneshwar's Jnaneshwari — Marathi literature arrives
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Palkuriki Somanatha; Telugu devotional literature
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The iqta assignment ties military service to revenue and not to land
events.evidence: The Sultanate's own administrative literature and the transfer records of assignments between officers.
events.note: Pay an officer with the tax of a district, and move him before he puts down roots. It is a solution to the same problem the mandala answers differently.

events.title: Jnaneshwar puts the Gita into Marathi and is expelled for it
events.evidence: The Jnaneshwari itself, and the tradition of his family's excommunication.

events.title: The silver tanka and the copper jital set a currency for the north
events.evidence: The Sultanate mint series, and Barani's account of the market regulations priced in them.

events.title: Amir Khusrau writes in Persian and in Hindavi
events.evidence: The five divans, the Khamsa, and the Hindavi verses attributed to him.

events.title: Alauddin's market controls
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Alauddin Khalji raids Devagiri and finds the Deccan open
events.evidence: Barani and Amir Khusrau, and the sudden appearance of Deccan bullion in Delhi's coinage.
events.becomes: The southern campaigns that follow, the Tughlaq capital at Daulatabad, and — indirectly — Vijayanagara, founded by men who had served in Delhi.

events.title: Mongol invasions repelled
events.evidence: Inscriptions, coinage, and chronicles — usually the victor's.
events.becomes: nothing

events.title: The Sultanate turns back six Mongol invasions in twenty years
events.evidence: Barani's account of the campaigns and of Alauddin's standing army and price controls.
events.becomes: A permanent paid army, the market regulations that fed it, and a fiscal apparatus reaching into village grain prices — built to fight Mongols and then used to conquer the Deccan.

events.title: Gujarat is annexed to Delhi and then goes independent
events.evidence: The Sultanate records and the Gujarat sultanate's own coinage from 1407.
events.becomes: An independent Gujarat sultanate, Ahmedabad, and a naval policy that fought the Portuguese at Diu with an Egyptian fleet.

events.title: Namdev; the Varkari pilgrimage to Pandharpur
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Odishan diamond triangle monasteries wind down
events.evidence: Declining construction and endowment at Ratnagiri, Lalitagiri and Udayagiri; a slow ending rather than a fire.

events.title: Gond polities become kingdoms in their own right
events.evidence: Garha-Mandla and Chanda dynastic records, forts and coinage.
events.note: The frontier is not a permanent condition. A people the settled record filed as forest-dwellers built states, minted money and were treated as powers.

events.title: Namdev carries Marathi abhangas north into Punjab
events.evidence: His verses in both the Marathi tradition and the Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Cambay is the western ocean's greatest port until its creek silts
events.evidence: The Arab and European accounts, and the geomorphological evidence for the silting that moved the trade to Surat.

events.title: The prabandha chronicles record Gujarat's own past
events.evidence: The Prabandhachintamani and Prabandhakosha, written by Jain monks about kings and merchants.

events.title: The Modi script is adopted for Marathi administration
events.evidence: The Modi document series, which runs from the Yadava period through the Peshwa archive into the twentieth century.
events.note: A cursive script designed to be written without lifting the pen. Millions of revenue documents are in it and most have never been read.

events.title: The Gulf horse trade becomes the Deccan's largest import
events.evidence: The Vijayanagara and Bahmani accounts of purchase contracts, and Marco Polo and Abdur Razzaq on the numbers.
events.note: Horses do not breed well in the Deccan. Every cavalry army in the south was an import bill.

events.title: Alauddin fixes grain prices and builds the granaries to hold them
events.evidence: Barani's detailed account of the schedule, the state granaries, and the officers who enforced it.

events.title: The spinning wheel spreads and cotton output multiplies
events.evidence: The earliest Indian depictions and references, and the growth in cotton textile exports that follows.
events.note: A device that multiplies one person's output several times over. It arrives quietly and changes the export economy.

events.title: Alauddin takes Chittor
events.evidence: The Sultanate chronicles, Amir Khusrau's eyewitness account, and the fort's own inscriptions.
events.becomes: A siege that entered Rajput memory as the founding trauma, retold for six centuries — and much of what is now remembered about it was written three hundred years later.

events.title: The Yadavas end
events.evidence: Inscriptions dated in regnal years, coinage, and the dynastic lists that later chronicles compile from both.

events.title: Kakatiya falls: Warangal is taken by the Tughlaqs
events.evidence: The Delhi court histories, and the abrupt end of the Kakatiya inscription series.
events.becomes: The Kakatiya nayaka officers scatter south and become the Nayaka lineages of Madurai, Tanjore and Gingee — the administrative class survives the state by four hundred years.

events.title: The Reddi and Velama kingdoms hold the delta after the Kakatiyas
events.evidence: The Reddi and Velama inscription and literary records.

events.title: Daulatabad
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Daulatabad is cut into a rock cone and made a capital
events.evidence: The scarped rock face, the spiral tunnel, and the Delhi population that was marched there and back.

events.title: token currency fails
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.
events.note: A fiat currency in 1330. The idea was right; the anti-counterfeiting was not.

events.title: Chokhamela sings outside the temple he is not allowed to enter
events.evidence: His abhangas, and his samadhi's position at the threshold of the Pandharpur temple.

events.title: Ibn Battuta
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Deccan famine of the 1330s empties a new capital
events.evidence: Barani and Ibn Battuta, and the Sultanate's own relief measures and their failure.

events.title: The Madurai Sultanate holds the far south for forty years
events.evidence: Ibn Battuta, who was there and married into the ruling family, and the sultanate's coinage.
events.becomes: Vijayanagara's southern expansion is organised to remove it, and the Nayaka system of military governorship is built to hold what is taken.

events.title: Vijayanagara founded
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Kashmir Sultanate
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Shah Mir sultanate takes the valley
events.evidence: The Persian chronicles of Kashmir and the sultanate's coinage.
events.becomes: A Persianate court in the valley, the Kashmiri shawl industry organised under state patronage, and the papier-mache and carpet trades that came with craftsmen brought from Samarkand.

events.title: Madhava of Sangamagrama founds the Kerala school
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Vijayanagara is laid out across seven ranges of hills
events.evidence: The surviving urban core: the royal centre, the sacred centre, the aqueducts and the bazaar streets.

events.title: The Bahmani secession divides the Deccan for two centuries
events.evidence: The Bahmani coinage and court chronicles, and the Tughlaq record of the revolt.
events.becomes: Five successor sultanates, a Persianate court culture at Bijapur and Golconda, and Dakhni — a literary language before Urdu had a name.

events.title: paper displaces palm leaf — recopying costs collapse
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.

events.title: Lal Ded's vakhs pass into Kashmiri speech and stay there
events.evidence: The vakhs, transmitted orally for centuries before collection, and quoted as proverb.

events.title: The Srivaishnavas divide over whether grace requires effort
events.evidence: The Vadakalai and Tenkalai commentarial traditions, and the temple litigation between them.

events.title: The Kerala school runs for three centuries as a teaching lineage
events.evidence: The succession from Madhava through Parameshvara, Nilakantha, Jyesthadeva and Achyuta, documented in the texts themselves.
events.note: Not a lone genius. A named teaching lineage, teacher to student, for three hundred years.

events.title: Manipravalam and the Lilatilakam's grammar for a mixed language
events.evidence: The Lilatilakam, which sets out the rules for combining Sanskrit and Malayalam and argues for the result as literature.

events.title: The gopuram overtakes the vimana and temple towns grow outward
events.evidence: The building sequence at Srirangam, Madurai and Chidambaram, where later gateways exceed the sanctum tower in height.
events.note: The tallest thing stops being over the god and starts being at the edge of town. The temple has become a city.

events.title: Gaur and Pandua build a Bengal idiom in brick
events.evidence: The Adina mosque at Pandua and the brick and terracotta mosques of Gaur.

events.title: Paper displaces palm leaf, and the cost of a copy collapses
events.evidence: The shift in surviving manuscript supports, the paper mills recorded at Daulatabad and Kashmir, and the sudden growth in manuscript numbers after this date.
events.note: The single biggest change to the knowledge economy between writing and printing, and nobody fought a battle over it.

events.title: The Bengal Sultanate; a distinct literary patron
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Firuz Shah's canals water the Delhi hinterland
events.evidence: The Yamuna and Sutlej canal alignments, the Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi's account, and the later Mughal reuse of the same cuts.

events.title: Firuz Shah moves two Ashokan pillars to Delhi and asks what they say
events.evidence: The pillars, still standing at Firuz Shah Kotla and the Ridge, and the chronicle's account of the engineering.
events.note: Sixteen hundred years old already, and nobody could read them. It took another five centuries.

events.title: Sayana's commentary on the whole Rigveda, at the Vijayanagara court
events.evidence: The bhasya, undertaken with state support, and the colophons naming the patron.
events.note: A state paying for a complete commentary on a three-thousand-year-old text. That is the knowledge economy at full stretch.

events.title: Hindavi, Awadhi and Dakhni become written literary languages
events.evidence: The Chandayan of Maulana Daud, the Sufi premakhyan romances, and the Dakhni corpus of the Deccan courts.

events.title: Mallinatha's commentaries fix how the kavya is read
events.evidence: The commentaries on Kalidasa, Bharavi, Magha and Sri Harsha, which every later edition follows.

events.title: Jaunpur becomes a court that patronises in its own right
events.evidence: The Sharqi mosque architecture and the sultanate's manuscript patronage record.

events.title: The Durga Devi famine empties the Deccan
events.evidence: Persian and Marathi chronicle accounts of a famine lasting more than a decade. The duration is probably compressed memory of several.

events.title: Timur sacks Delhi and leaves within a fortnight
events.evidence: The Zafarnama, and Timur's own memoir, which counts the dead as an achievement.
events.becomes: The Sultanate's authority breaks and the regional sultanates — Jaunpur, Malwa, Gujarat, Bengal — become independent centres of patronage in their own languages.

events.title: Infinite series for π, sine and cosine — with proofs
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: The buranji chronicle tradition begins — history as state practice
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Kashmiri Sanskrit libraries are dispersed
events.evidence: Later Kashmiri accounts of manuscript loss; how much is contemporary record and how much later lament is hard to separate.
events.dispute_text: The scale of loss under the Sultanate is described very differently by different later sources, some of which have a position to defend. The event is real; its magnitude is argued.

events.title: The Little Ice Age begins and the monsoon weakens
events.evidence: Speleothem and tree-ring records; the correlation with the medieval famine sequence is strong.

events.title: The Indian Ocean carries the largest trading system in the world
events.evidence: The Chinese, Arab and Gujarati accounts, the Kerala and Coromandel port records, and the ceramic distributions.

events.title: Bhil support becomes decisive in Mewar's politics
events.evidence: Rajput chronicle tradition, which credits Bhil archers repeatedly and is not a neutral source about them.

events.title: Vijayanagara enlists forest chiefs as frontier garrisons
events.evidence: The nayaka system's absorption of local power-holders, some of whom held hill and forest tracts.

events.title: The Lingayat mathas become landholding institutions
events.evidence: The matha inscription and grant record across the Kannada country.

events.title: The Sant poets write in the spoken languages and refuse both orthodoxies
events.evidence: The verse of Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev, Dadu and Sena, transmitted in three separate written traditions.

events.title: Srinatha writes for four courts and describes each of them
events.evidence: His works and their dedications, and the court records that corroborate the patronage.

events.title: The mangalkavya: local goddesses, merchant voyages and Bengali verse
events.evidence: The Chandimangal and Manasamangal corpus and its manuscript tradition.

events.title: The Rishi order: Nund Rishi and a Kashmiri Sufism with local roots
events.evidence: The shruks of Nund Rishi, and the shrine network of the order.
events.note: It grew out of Lal Ded's verse as much as out of Persian Sufism. The valley made its own.

events.title: Temple destruction under Sikandar, and the argument about its scale
events.evidence: The Persian chronicles, which claim it; the surviving temples, which complicate it; and Jonaraja's continuation of the Rajatarangini.

events.title: Calicut's Zamorin runs an open port and lets the Arab merchants police it
events.evidence: Ma Huan's and Abdur Razzaq's accounts, and the Portuguese descriptions of the arrangements they displaced.

events.title: Cinnamon becomes the island's export and then its problem
events.evidence: The Arab and Chinese trade records, and the Portuguese monopoly that followed.

events.title: Kotte, Jaffna and Kandy: three kingdoms on one island
events.evidence: The Sinhala and Tamil chronicle traditions and the Portuguese accounts of all three.

events.title: Dingal and Charan bardic poetry becomes the state's memory
events.evidence: The Charan bardic corpus, the khyat chronicles, and the courts that maintained the poets.
events.note: A caste of professional rememberers on a state salary. The knowledge economy with a job description.

events.title: Arunagirinathar's Tiruppugazh sets Tamil devotion to complex rhythm
events.evidence: The Tiruppugazh corpus and its metrical schemes, still used as a percussion training text.

events.title: Vijayanagara's water system supplies a city in a dry granite basin
events.evidence: The Kamalapuram tank, the aqueduct channels and the stepped tank of dressed schist brought from elsewhere.

events.title: Mandu's plateau city and its water architecture
events.evidence: The Jahaz Mahal between two tanks, the Hindola Mahal and the twelve-kilometre wall circuit.

events.title: Bengali literature acquires a court under the Sultanate
events.evidence: The Srikrishnakirtan manuscript, and the Sultanate's patronage of Bengali translations of the Sanskrit epics.
events.note: A Muslim court paid for the first Bengali Mahabharata. The obvious story is the wrong one.

events.title: Vidyapati writes in Maithili and is read across the east
events.evidence: The padavali corpus, and its adoption into the Bengali and Assamese Vaishnava traditions.

events.title: Malwa's sultanate builds at Mandu and cooks a book about it
events.evidence: The Ni'matnama, a cookery manuscript illustrated for the Malwa court, and the Mandu building sequence.
events.note: An illustrated recipe book is state records too. It records what a court ate, and who cooked.

events.title: Zheng He's fleets call at Calicut, Cochin and Bengal
events.evidence: The Chinese voyage records, the Ma Huan account, and the trilingual Galle stele.

events.title: The Gujarat Sultanate and the rise of Ahmedabad
events.evidence: The city's foundation inscription, and the Gujarati and Persian building record.

events.title: Ramananda takes disciples without regard to birth
events.evidence: The Bhaktamal tradition and the disciple lists that name Ravidas, Kabir and Sena.

events.title: Zain-ul-Abidin reverses the policy and has the Sanskrit texts recopied
events.evidence: Jonaraja and Srivara's chronicles, and the translation projects into Persian he commissioned.
events.note: Called Budshah, the great king, four hundred years later and still. He rebuilt what his father's reign had burned.

events.title: Kumaravyasa's Kannada Mahabharata, sung rather than read
events.evidence: The text, and the gamaka recitation tradition that still performs it.

events.title: The Gajapatis
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: Kabir
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Sankardev; the Ekasarana movement and Assamese literature
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Vijayanagara's aqueducts and tanks supply a city of a quarter million
events.evidence: The surviving aqueduct channels, the Kamalapuram tank, and Abdur Razzaq's and Paes's descriptions of the city.

events.title: Annamacharya's keertanas are engraved on copper and sealed in a wall
events.evidence: The copper plates recovered from the Tirumala temple in 1922, some thirteen thousand songs.
events.note: Sealed in a room for four hundred years. Redundancy by accident.

events.title: The Haridasa movement sets devotion to a teachable musical form
events.evidence: The devaranama corpus of Purandara and Kanaka Dasa, and the Udupi matha's records.

events.title: Sarala Das writes the Mahabharata in Odia, and is not a brahmin
events.evidence: The text, whose author names himself a sudra and a farmer, and the manuscript tradition.

events.title: Srirangapatna is fortified on its river island
events.evidence: The island fort's earliest bastions, later rebuilt under Tipu Sultan.

events.title: The Damajipant famine
events.evidence: Chronicle and hagiographical accounts; the date is traditional.

events.title: Guru Nanak
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Ravidas describes Begampura, a city without sorrow or tax or caste
events.evidence: His verses in the Guru Granth Sahib and the Rajasthani manuscript tradition.
events.note: A leatherworker describes a city with no grading of men. It is a utopia, and it is a critique.

events.title: Sankardev's Ekasarana and the namghar as a village institution
events.evidence: The borgeet and ankiya nat corpus, and the namghar network across the Brahmaputra valley.
events.note: A prayer house that is also the village assembly. Devotion with a constitution.

events.title: Kabir's dohas circulate before anyone writes them down
events.evidence: Three separate written traditions — the Bijak, the Guru Granth Sahib and the Rajasthani manuscripts — which do not agree.
events.note: Three recensions that disagree is what an oral corpus looks like when it finally hits paper.

events.title: Champaner is built below Pavagadh as a Gujarat capital
events.evidence: The Jama Masjid, the helical stepwells and the surviving town walls.

events.title: Chaitanya
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar build a Deccan court idiom
events.evidence: The building sequences of the three sultanates, and the Dakhni literary record they patronised.

events.title: Vasco da Gama at Calicut
events.evidence: Company and government records, which are voluminous and interested.

events.title: Shipbuilding and construction raise the demand for hardwood
events.evidence: Teak in Indian Ocean shipbuilding and in Portuguese and Dutch procurement records.

events.title: Cabral bombards Calicut and the licensed sea begins
events.evidence: The Portuguese accounts, and the Zamorin's alliance with the Egyptian and Gujarati fleets that followed.
events.becomes: Diu in 1509, and after it three centuries in which Indian shipping sails at somebody else's permission.

events.title: Kabir refuses both temple and mosque, and both claim him after
events.evidence: The three recensions of his verse, and the tradition that both communities claimed the body.

events.title: Nanak makes the shared kitchen a condition of the congregation
events.evidence: The institution of langar and pangat, and the janamsakhi accounts of Nanak eating with whoever came.

events.title: The Golconda mines are the world's only diamond source
events.evidence: Tavernier's account of visiting the mines, and the European trade records.

events.title: Dhaka muslin is woven at thread counts nobody has since matched
events.evidence: The surviving pieces, the Mughal and European purchase records, and the nineteenth-century attempts to reproduce it.
events.note: The cotton it needed went extinct. The technique went with it.

events.title: The Kashmir shawl becomes a global luxury export
events.evidence: The workshop records, the European inventories, and the French and Scottish imitations that followed.

events.title: The Panchasakha take devotion into Odia and out of Sanskrit
events.evidence: The five poets' works and their manuscript transmission.

events.title: Nilakantha's Tantrasangraha
events.evidence: The text, dated by its own chronogram to 1501, with the series expansions of the Kerala school.

events.title: The cartaz: the Indian Ocean becomes a licensed sea
events.evidence: The Portuguese pass registers, and the Mughal and Gujarati correspondence about ships stopped for want of one.
events.note: For a thousand years the ocean was open. From here you sail with someone's permission.

events.title: An earthquake destroys towns across the Himalayan front
events.evidence: Persian chronicle accounts and later palaeoseismic trenching along the Himalayan frontal thrust.

events.title: The Portuguese take the coast and cannot take the highlands
events.evidence: The Portuguese records, and the Kandyan accounts of the campaigns that failed.
events.becomes: A Catholic coastal population, a Portuguese-derived creole, and a Kandyan kingdom that survives by being unreachable — for another three hundred years.

events.title: Diu: the Portuguese defeat a combined Gujarati, Egyptian and Calicut fleet
events.evidence: The Portuguese and Egyptian accounts of the action.
events.becomes: Portuguese naval supremacy in the western Indian Ocean, and the cartaz system that followed from it.

events.title: The Portuguese take Goa and hold it for four and a half centuries
events.evidence: The Portuguese chancery records, and the Goa Inquisition's own archive.
events.becomes: The cartaz pass system, which made the Indian Ocean a licensed sea for the first time; the Konkani printing press; and an Inquisition that burned Konkani and Marathi manuscripts as well as people.

events.title: Chaitanya's kirtan takes devotion into the street
events.evidence: The Chaitanya Charitamrita, and the Bengal Vaishnava institutional record.

events.title: the Kerala school's infinite series
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Mirabai leaves a court to sing, and the court cannot get her back
events.evidence: Her padas in the Rajasthani and Braj traditions, and their inclusion in the Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Purandara Dasa sets the Carnatic teaching sequence still used
events.evidence: The graded exercises attributed to him, which every student still begins with.

events.title: The Sikh panth takes institutional form: sangat, langar, and a line of Gurus
events.evidence: The janamsakhis, the Goindval pothis, and the succession from Nanak.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya writes the Amuktamalyada, and it contains advice on statecraft
events.evidence: The text, whose chapters on how to treat merchants and forest peoples read as policy.
events.note: An emperor's poem that tells you to keep the forest peoples on your side because they know the roads.

events.title: First Panipat: field artillery decides a battle in India
events.evidence: The Baburnama, which describes the tulughma and the carts chained together, and the Lodi coinage that stops.
events.becomes: The Mughal empire, the Ain-i-Akbari's revenue survey, a workshop tradition in painting, and the argument about sovereignty that Akbar's court conducted in public.

events.title: Babur writes the Baburnama in Chagatai
events.evidence: The Chagatai text, with its gaps, its botany and its account of the author's own failures.
events.note: An emperor's memoir that records losing. It also catalogues the fruit.

events.title: The Madurai and Tanjore Nayakas inherit Vijayanagara's south
events.evidence: The Nayaka records, the Mackenzie manuscript collections, and the temple building programmes.

events.title: Lepakshi's murals are painted on a Vijayanagara ceiling
events.evidence: The Virabhadra temple's painted ceiling, the largest surviving pre-modern mural cycle in south India.

events.title: Jyesthadeva's Yuktibhasha: the proofs, in Malayalam
events.evidence: The text, which gives demonstrations rather than results — and is written in the spoken language, not Sanskrit.
events.note: Calculus results with proofs, in a regional language, a century before Newton.

events.title: The Koch kingdom and Naranarayana's patronage of Assamese
events.evidence: The Koch records, and the Vaishnava manuscript production under Naranarayana.

events.title: Sher Shah's rupiya, road and revenue survey
events.evidence: The rupiya itself, still the unit; the Grand Trunk Road's sarais; and the zabt measurement records.
events.note: Five years in power. The currency, the road and the survey all outlast the empire that replaced him.

events.title: The Banjara carriers move the grain that feeds every army
events.evidence: Mughal and Maratha campaign records of contracted bullock trains, and the European accounts of caravans in the tens of thousands.
events.note: Nobody's subjects, everybody's logistics. An army moved at the speed the Banjaras agreed to.

events.title: Ezhuthachan fixes the Malayalam script and the language's literary form
events.evidence: The Adhyatmaramayanam kilippattu and the script reform attributed to him.

events.title: Cast artillery and matchlocks change what a fort is for
events.evidence: The surviving guns, the siege accounts, and the change in fortification profile after this date.

events.title: The Goa Inquisition opens and runs for two hundred and fifty years
events.evidence: The Inquisition's own records, and the prohibition of Konkani in public that accompanied it.

events.title: Talikota, and Vijayanagara is emptied
events.evidence: Ferishta and the Portuguese accounts, and the burnt layer across the city's excavated core.
events.becomes: The Deccan sultanates inherit the south, and the Nayaka successor states inherit Vijayanagara's temple and irrigation administration and run it for another two centuries.

events.title: The Keladi and Mysore Wodeyar lines inherit Vijayanagara's administration
events.evidence: The Keladi and Mysore records, and the continuity of the nayankara assignment system.

events.title: Odisha is annexed to the Mughal empire
events.evidence: The Akbarnama and the Afghan and Gajapati accounts.
events.becomes: The Jagannath temple's administration passes through Afghan, Mughal, Maratha and finally British hands — and every one of them kept it running, because the pilgrim revenue was worth more than the point.

events.title: Mewar refuses the Mughal marriage alliance the other houses accept
events.evidence: The Mughal court records of who submitted and when, and the Mewar chronicles.

events.title: Fatehpur Sikri is built, occupied, and left within fifteen years
events.evidence: The complete surviving city, and the Mughal chronicles that record its abandonment.
events.note: A capital built from nothing and empty in a generation, most likely for want of water.

events.title: Tulsidas writes the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi
events.evidence: The text, which dates its own beginning, and the manuscript tradition from Varanasi.

events.title: Akbar's debating hall puts Jesuits, Jains, Zoroastrians and ulema in one room
events.evidence: The Ibadat Khana accounts in the Akbarnama and the Jesuit letters from the mission, which agree about the arguments and not the outcomes.

events.title: Tamil printing begins earlier than any other Indian language
events.evidence: The Thambiran Vanakkam, printed at Quilon in 1578, and the Tranquebar press that followed.
events.note: The first book printed in an Indian script came off a press in India in 1578. Not 1800.

events.title: The imperial hunt claims the forest as a royal preserve
events.evidence: The Ain-i-Akbari and Mughal painting, in which the qamargah hunt is an assertion of sovereignty over ground and over the people who live on it.

events.title: Surat's pilgrim shipping runs on Mughal and Gujarati capital
events.evidence: The port records, the imperial ships Rahimi and Ganj-i-Sawai, and the cartaz passes they had to carry.

events.title: The zabt settlement measures land and prices it by a ten-year average
events.evidence: The Ain-i-Akbari's revenue tables, district by district and crop by crop.

events.title: The imperial atelier makes painting a documented profession
events.evidence: The signed and attributed folios, and the Ain-i-Akbari's list of the leading painters by name.

events.title: Eknath edits the Jnaneshwari and settles its text
events.evidence: His recension, which is the basis of every later edition, and his own colophon explaining why it was needed.
events.note: Three hundred years after it was written, somebody sat down and fixed the text. That is the corpus mechanic performed by hand.

events.title: The Mughals annex the valley and build gardens in it
events.evidence: The Akbarnama, and the Shalimar and Nishat garden records.

events.title: Madhavdev's Namghosa and the sattra manuscript workshops
events.evidence: The sanchipat manuscripts on aloe bark, and the sattra libraries that still hold them.
events.note: They wrote on aloe bark treated to last. Some of those manuscripts are four hundred years old and still legible.

events.title: the Ain-i-Akbari
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.
events.note: The most detailed statistical account of any pre-modern state anywhere. It is also propaganda. Both are true.

events.title: The Odishan hill communities hold their own tracts
events.evidence: Later Company records describe long-established autonomy; the earlier centuries are inferred from that.

events.title: Forest tracts are written into revenue settlements
events.evidence: Mughal revenue records assigning forested parganas to zamindars.

events.title: Arakanese and Portuguese raiders depopulate the Bengal delta
events.evidence: The Mughal and Portuguese accounts of the Sandwip and Chittagong raids, and the Bengali literature that records them.
events.becomes: The Mughal conquest of Chittagong in 1666, and a frontier of forest clearance and settlement that reshaped eastern Bengal.

events.title: Coromandel kalamkari and painted cottons reach Europe and Southeast Asia
events.evidence: The Dutch and English factory orders with their pattern specifications, and the surviving textiles.

events.title: Surat and Bharuch shipyards build for Indian, Mughal and European owners
events.evidence: The shipyard records, the teak supply contracts, and the European purchases of Indian-built hulls.
events.note: The Bombay Dockyard built ships for the Royal Navy. One of them is still afloat.

events.title: Dholavira is reoccupied briefly, and left again
events.evidence: Stage VII at the site: crude round houses built over the ruins of the planned town.
events.note: Somebody came back, lived in the ruins, and left. Nobody knows who.

events.title: Masulipatnam becomes the Coromandel's chintz port
events.evidence: Dutch and English factory records, and the kalamkari workshops of the hinterland.

events.title: Surat becomes the Mughal empire's sea gate
events.evidence: The customs house records, the English and Dutch factories, and the pilgrim traffic to the Red Sea.

events.title: Silver from the Americas flows into India and stays there
events.evidence: The Mughal mint output series, and the European accounts complaining about a trade balance that only went one way.

events.title: The East India Company is chartered, and the Dutch and French follow
events.evidence: The charters themselves, and the factory records that begin immediately after.

events.title: The Adi Granth is compiled, and later sealed as the Guru
events.evidence: The Kartarpur manuscript, and the 1708 declaration that the book itself succeeds the human Gurus.
events.note: It includes Hindu and Muslim voices alongside the Gurus'. The canon is deliberately not one community's.

events.title: The Ahoms defeat seventeen Mughal invasions and record every one
events.evidence: The buranjis, which are state chronicles kept as an administrative duty, and the Mughal accounts that agree about the outcomes.
events.becomes: Assam is never annexed. The paik labour system that raised the armies survives, and so does the chronicle tradition — history as state practice, which no other Indian polity institutionalised.

events.title: The Mewar and Marwar painting workshops
events.evidence: The dated and signed folios, and the workshop records of the Udaipur and Jodhpur courts.

events.title: The Deccan famine of 1630 kills across three provinces
events.evidence: Peter Mundy's eyewitness account on the road to Surat, the Mughal relief records, and the Dutch factory correspondence.

events.title: The Deccan and Gujarat famine
events.evidence: Mughal court records and Dutch and English factory correspondence, which agree on its severity.

events.title: Tukaram's abhangas
events.evidence: The abhanga corpus and the Dehu manuscript tradition.

events.title: The Taj Mahal is built, and the accounts survive
events.evidence: The building accounts, the craftsmen's wage records, and the completion inscription.
events.note: Late. For ninety-five per cent of this campaign it does not exist, which is why it is not on the map.

events.title: Madras, Bombay and Calcutta are founded as company towns
events.evidence: The Company's grants and fort records for Fort St George, the Bombay marriage transfer, and the Sutanuti purchase.

events.title: The Padshahnama is compiled and illustrated
events.evidence: The manuscript and its paintings, and the succession of court historians named in it.

events.title: The Maunder minimum and a run of failed monsoons
events.evidence: Solar and speleothem records, and the clustering of famine in the Mughal and Deccan archives.

events.title: Shahjahanabad is laid out with its bazaar on a canal
events.evidence: The walled city, the Chandni Chowk canal alignment, and the imperial building accounts.

events.title: Kathakali takes form out of older temple theatre
events.evidence: The attakatha texts and the Kottarakkara and Kottayam court records.

events.title: Marwari merchant houses build a credit network across the subcontinent
events.evidence: The hundi records, the firm ledgers, and the branch correspondence between Rajasthan, Bengal and the Deccan.
events.note: A bill of exchange honoured two thousand kilometres away, on trust and a family name. The trade system's top rung.

events.title: Hugli, Chinsurah and the Bengal river factories
events.evidence: Portuguese, Dutch, French and Danish factory sites along a forty-kilometre stretch of one river.

events.title: Indian cotton textiles become the world's largest manufactured export
events.evidence: The Company shipping records, the Dutch VOC accounts, and the English legislation passed to keep the cloth out.
events.note: England banned it. That is how big it was.

events.title: Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar
events.evidence: The text, and the works that quote or answer it.

events.title: Dara Shikoh has fifty Upanishads translated into Persian
events.evidence: The Sirr-i-Akbar manuscript, and the Latin version made from it that reached Schopenhauer.
events.note: A Mughal prince's Persian Upanishads become Europe's first Upanishads, via Latin, in 1801.

events.title: The Dutch replace the Portuguese and codify the law
events.evidence: The VOC records, and the Roman-Dutch law still in force in parts of the island.
events.becomes: Roman-Dutch law, the Thesawalamai and Muslim personal law codified alongside it, and a canal system in the southwest that is still in use.

events.title: The Sahyadri hill communities and the fort system
events.evidence: The Maratha hill forts and the local communities who garrisoned and supplied them, named in Marathi records as groups rather than individuals.

events.title: Shivaji sacks Surat and shows the empire is porous
events.evidence: The English and Dutch factory records, which describe the raid from inside the city.
events.becomes: A revenue system built on chauth and sardeshmukhi — a claim on somebody else's tax rather than a conquest of their land, which is far cheaper to enforce and much harder to remove.

events.title: Lachit Barphukan wins Saraighat on the river
events.evidence: The buranjis and the Mughal accounts of the fleet action at the Brahmaputra narrows.
events.becomes: The Mughal frontier stops at the Manas. Assam stays outside the empire until the Company arrives a century and a half later.

events.title: The Satnami rising: peasants and leatherworkers against the empire
events.evidence: The Mughal court accounts of the revolt near Narnaul and its suppression.

events.title: Shivaji crowned
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Tanjore Marathas keep a Sanskrit and Tamil library and catalogue it
events.evidence: The Sarasvati Mahal collection and Serfoji II's catalogues.

events.title: Aurangzeb spends twenty-six years in the Deccan
events.evidence: The Mughal court histories, the campaign correspondence, and the collapse of the jagir assignment system it produced.
events.becomes: The Deccan is annexed and the empire is bankrupted doing it. The Marathas the campaign was meant to destroy hold the initiative within a decade of its end.

events.title: the Khalsa
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Khalsa is instituted at Anandpur
events.evidence: The Sikh chronicles and the surviving hukamnamas.

events.title: The Thanjavur collection is catalogued and kept
events.evidence: The Maratha rulers' cataloguing of the palace library, which is why it survived.

events.title: The Ahom maidams and the Rangpur palace complex
events.evidence: The burial mounds at Charaideo and the surviving brick structures at Sivasagar.

events.title: Aurangzeb dies
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: The Sikh misls hold the Punjab between empires
events.evidence: The misl records and the coin legends struck in the Gurus' name.

events.title: The Peshwas run the Maratha confederacy from Pune
events.evidence: The Peshwa Daftar, some four crore documents, still the largest indigenous administrative archive in India.
events.note: The archive alone is the reason the eighteenth century in India can be written from Indian sources.

events.title: The Bengal nawabs make the province the empire's richest
events.evidence: The Murshidabad revenue records and the Company's own estimates of Bengal's remittances to Delhi.

events.title: Chauth and sardeshmukhi become a subcontinental revenue claim
events.evidence: The Maratha revenue records and the treaties conceding the claim from Bengal to the Carnatic.

events.title: The Gaekwads take Baroda and hold it into the twentieth century
events.evidence: The Maratha and Company records, and the Baroda state archive.

events.title: The Nizam's dominions become the largest princely state
events.evidence: The Asaf Jahi records and the subsidiary treaty of 1798.

events.title: Marthanda Varma builds Travancore and dedicates it to a god
events.evidence: The Travancore state records and the Trippadidanam of 1750.

events.title: A great storm and shock strike Bengal
events.evidence: European trading records; the casualty figures that circulated were later shown to be inflated by an order of magnitude.
events.dispute_text: Contemporary reports conflate a cyclone with an earthquake said to have struck the same night. Modern seismology finds no evidence of a large earthquake, and the event as usually described probably did not happen.

events.title: A cyclone and surge destroy the Hooghly shipping
events.evidence: English and Dutch trading records of shipping losses in the Hooghly, written up months afterwards and at second hand.
events.dispute_text: Contemporary accounts conflate a cyclone with an earthquake reported the same night, and the casualty figures that circulated were later shown to be wildly inflated.

events.title: Nadir Shah takes Delhi and the treasury with it
events.evidence: The Persian and Mughal court accounts, and the disappearance of the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor from the Indian record.
events.becomes: Mughal solvency ends. The provinces stop remitting, the Marathas, the Nizam and Awadh become the real powers, and the Company acquires an opening it did not have to fight for.

events.title: The Carnatic wars are fought by Indian armies under European officers
events.evidence: The Company and Compagnie records, and the subsidiary treaties with the Nizam and the Nawab of Arcot.
events.becomes: The sepoy army and the subsidiary alliance: a ruler pays for troops he does not command, and loses his revenue and then his state to the arrangement.

events.title: The Marathas take coastal Odisha and tax the pilgrim road
events.evidence: The Nagpur Bhonsle records and the Jagannath temple's pilgrim tax accounts.

events.title: The ordination lineage is re-imported from Siam
events.evidence: The Siyam Nikaya's own records, and the Siamese mission's account.
events.note: The island had given Buddhism to Southeast Asia. It got its ordination line back from Thailand twelve centuries later.

events.title: Plassey, and then the Diwani
events.evidence: The Company's own correspondence, the treaty with Mir Jafar, and the 1765 grant of the diwani of Bengal.
events.becomes: A trading company acquires the revenue of a province and stops having to ship bullion to buy Indian goods. The Drain opens, and it is an accounting fact before it is a policy.

events.title: Third Panipat
events.evidence: The Maratha and Afghan accounts, and the correspondence of the Peshwa's camp before and after.
events.becomes: Maratha expansion north stops. Neither victor holds Delhi. The vacuum is filled four years later at Buxar, by a trading company.

events.title: Haidar Ali takes Mysore and builds a modern army out of it
events.evidence: The Mysore state records, the French officers' accounts, and the Company's assessments.

events.title: Buxar settles what Plassey only started
events.evidence: The battle accounts, and the Treaty of Allahabad that followed a year later.
events.becomes: The Mughal emperor grants the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to a company. Sovereignty and revenue separate, and the Company holds the half that pays.

events.title: The Company takes the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
events.evidence: The Treaty of Allahabad, and the Company's revenue accounts from the following year.
events.note: The point at which a trading company stops paying for Indian goods with silver and starts paying with Indian taxes.

events.title: The Mysore wars: four of them, and the last one ends the state
events.evidence: The Company records, the Mysore court correspondence, and the rocket artillery the British took back to Woolwich.
events.becomes: Congreve rockets, developed at Woolwich from Mysorean examples; and, in India, the annexation model that the Company then applied everywhere.

events.title: The Moamoria rebellion breaks the Ahom state from inside
events.evidence: The buranjis' own account, and the Company correspondence about the appeal for help.
events.note: Seventeen Mughal invasions failed. A peasant rebellion succeeded, and then the Burmese walked in.

events.title: the Great Bengal Famine
events.evidence: Destruction layers, and accounts written afterwards by people with a position.
events.note: Revenue collection was held steady while a third of the province died. The records are the Company's own.

events.title: The Anglo-Maratha wars end the last power that could have won
events.evidence: The Company and Peshwa records, and the treaties of Salbai, Bassein and Poona.
events.becomes: Paramountcy: after 1818 no Indian state can make war or foreign policy, and the map stops being a map of states and becomes a map of dependencies.

events.title: Mysorean iron-cased rockets are used in the field
events.evidence: The surviving examples taken to Woolwich, and the British accounts of Pollilur.
events.note: Iron casings, not paper. The British took specimens home and Congreve's rockets came out of them.

events.title: colonial manuscript removal — displacement, not destruction
events.evidence: Company and government records, which are voluminous and interested.

events.title: Manuscript collecting begins under the Company
events.evidence: The founding of the Asiatic Society and the collection registers that follow.
events.note: Displacement is not destruction, and the distinction matters mechanically: a work that leaves survives.

events.title: The Asiatic Society, and the discovery that the languages are related
events.evidence: The Society's Asiatick Researches, and Jones's 1786 address on Sanskrit, Greek and Latin.

events.title: The Doji bara, the skull famine
events.evidence: Company records; and it is one of the earliest famines that can be tied to a documented El Nino event.

events.title: The Permanent Settlement fixes Bengal's revenue for ever
events.evidence: The regulations, and the sale records of estates auctioned for arrears in the decades after.
events.note: Land that nobody owned individually became land somebody owned. The people using it became trespassers by paperwork.

events.title: Sarnath is quarried for a canal
events.evidence: Jagat Singh's removal of the stupa's brick, recorded by contemporaries who arrived too late to stop it.

events.title: Amaravati's stupa is quarried for building stone
events.evidence: Company records of the removal, and the sculptures now distributed between Chennai, London and elsewhere.
events.note: Not destruction by an invader. A local zamindar wanted lime and an antiquarian wanted marbles.

events.title: The Chuar risings in the Bengal uplands
events.evidence: Company military and revenue correspondence, which is the only side of it that survives in writing.

events.title: Mysore is restored to the Wodeyars as a subsidiary state
events.evidence: The partition treaty of Seringapatam and the subsidiary alliance that followed.

events.title: Srirangapatna falls and the Mysore capital moves
events.evidence: The breach in the north wall, and the East India Company's own account of the storming.

events.title: Printing begins to make loss reversible
events.evidence: Serampore and Fort William press output; a printed text can be lost from every library and still exist.
events.note: The first technology in seven thousand years that breaks the link between a work and its carriers.

events.title: Printing in the Indian scripts becomes cheap and general
events.evidence: The Serampore press output, the Fort William College texts, and the vernacular newspaper record that follows.
events.note: From here a work can stop being lost. It is the first time that has ever been true.

events.title: Fort William College commissions Bengali and Hindustani prose
events.evidence: The College's publication list and the munshis and pandits it employed by name.

events.title: The Great Trigonometrical Survey measures the subcontinent
events.evidence: The survey's own records, the Everest and Lambton triangulation data, and the Indian computers — Radhanath Sikdar among them — who did the arithmetic.
events.note: The most accurate survey on earth at the time. It was also how you tax and how you move an army.

events.title: The Channar revolt: the right to cover the upper body
events.evidence: The Travancore proclamations of 1829 and 1859 and the missionary and state correspondence.

events.title: The Mackenzie collection removes thousands of manuscripts
events.evidence: The collection catalogue, which lists what was gathered and from where.

events.title: Kandy falls and the whole island is under one authority
events.evidence: The Kandyan Convention, signed by the chiefs, and the 1818 rebellion that followed it.
events.becomes: Plantation agriculture — coffee, then tea — and the Indian Tamil labour brought in to work it, whose citizenship was still being argued about in the twentieth century.

events.title: The Burmese occupy Assam
events.evidence: The Burmese and Ahom accounts, and the Company's casus belli for the first Anglo-Burmese war.
events.becomes: The Treaty of Yandabo, annexation to British India, and the tea industry that followed within a decade.

events.title: Kannada printing, dictionaries and the modern prose sentence
events.evidence: The Serampore and Basel Mission presses, Kittel's dictionary of 1894, and the newspaper record.

events.title: Travancore and Cochin fund schooling, and literacy climbs early
events.evidence: The royal rescript of 1817 on state-funded education, and the census literacy series that follows.
events.note: A state deciding in 1817 that it would pay to teach everyone. The results are still visible in the numbers.

events.title: The Bhil risings against the new revenue order
events.evidence: Company records of successive campaigns and of the Bhil Corps raised to police them.

events.title: The Rajput states sign subsidiary treaties and stop being sovereign
events.evidence: The treaties themselves and the Rajputana Agency's records.

events.title: The Allah Bund earthquake reshapes Kutch
events.evidence: Company survey records and the fault scarp itself, which dammed a river and created a lake.

events.title: Indian textile manufacturing collapses against Lancashire
events.evidence: The trade series: cloth exports falling and yarn imports rising, and the census occupational data on weavers.

events.title: Ryotwari and mahalwari: two other ways to make land pay
events.evidence: The Madras and North-Western Provinces settlement reports, and Munro's and Wingate's own accounts of the survey method.

events.title: Malayalam printing, dictionaries and the first newspapers
events.evidence: The CMS Press at Kottayam, Gundert's dictionary of 1872, and the Rajyasamacharam files.

events.title: The Burmese wars and the annexation of Assam and Arakan
events.evidence: The Treaty of Yandabo, and the Company's revenue settlement of Assam that followed it.
events.becomes: Assam's tea plantations, the indentured labour brought in to work them, and a demographic change that is still politically live.

events.title: The Brahmo Samaj argues for reform from inside the texts
events.evidence: The Samaj's trust deed, and Rammohan Roy's translations and tracts.

events.title: Sati is prohibited by regulation, after argument on both sides in Sanskrit
events.evidence: Bengal Regulation XVII, and the petitions for and against, several of them citing the same texts.

events.title: James Tod writes the Annals and fixes a version of Rajput history
events.evidence: The Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan, and the bardic sources he used and did not always distinguish from record.

events.title: Indenture carries a million and a half people overseas
events.evidence: The emigration passes, the depot records, and the colonial commissions of inquiry.

events.title: Macaulay's Minute settles what language education happens in
events.evidence: The Minute itself, and the English Education Act that followed within months.
events.note: He had read none of the literature he dismissed and said so. The policy stood for a century.

events.title: Assamese is replaced by Bengali as the official language, and then restored
events.evidence: The government orders of 1836 and 1873, and the Orunodoi newspaper campaign in between.
events.note: A language removed from its own province by administrative order, and argued back by a newspaper.

events.title: Fire destroys much of Surat
events.evidence: Company records of the fire and of the merchant records lost with the warehouses.

events.title: The Agra famine
events.evidence: Company revenue and relief records.

events.title: The Khond risings
events.evidence: Company records of the Meriah agency campaigns.

events.title: Assam tea is planted and a labour system is built to pick it
events.evidence: The Assam Company records, the indenture contracts, and the labour commission reports.

events.title: The Coringa cyclone
