events.evidence: Company records of the destruction of the port, which was never rebuilt to its former size.

events.title: The Anglo-Sikh wars take the Punjab, the last independent state
events.evidence: The campaign records, the Treaty of Lahore, and the annexation proclamation of 1849.
events.becomes: The subcontinent is under one authority for the first time since Aurangzeb. Eight years later it rebels.

events.title: The Treaty of Amritsar sells the valley to the Dogras
events.evidence: The treaty itself, which names the sum, and the Company's correspondence about it.
events.note: A territory transferred by sale between two other parties. The game should let the player feel what that means.

events.title: Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule open a school for girls and for the excluded
events.evidence: The school records at Bhide Wada, Pune, and Gulamgiri, published 1873.
events.note: A woman teaching, in 1848, in a country where most men could not read.

events.title: railway and telegraph
events.evidence: Material remains — the object, its composition, and an absolute date where one exists.

events.title: The Thanjavur palace library passes into state hands
events.evidence: The transfer records; the collection survived where many private ones did not.

events.title: The Santhal hul
events.evidence: Company records, the trial proceedings, and Santhal oral accounts collected later.
events.note: Tens of thousands rose against moneylenders and the revenue settlement, two years before 1857, and it was put down with artillery.

events.title: Jute becomes Bengal's cash crop and Dundee's raw material
events.evidence: The mill records, the acreage returns, and the price series through both world wars.

events.title: The Widow Remarriage Act, argued through the shastras
events.evidence: Act XV of 1856, and Vidyasagar's tracts marshalling scriptural authority for it.

events.title: Caldwell argues the southern languages are a family of their own
events.evidence: The Comparative Grammar of the Dravidian Languages, and the linguistic evidence it assembled.

events.title: The Rebellion, and the Crown takes over from the Company
events.evidence: The military and civil records of both sides, the trial of Bahadur Shah, and the Government of India Act 1858.
events.becomes: Direct Crown rule, the end of annexation by doctrine of lapse, a permanent garrison ratio, and a colonial state that from then on governs by census, survey and category.

events.title: Crown rule replaces the Company
events.evidence: The Government of India Act 1858, and the Queen's Proclamation.

events.title: Paramountcy: five hundred and sixty-five states that are not sovereign and not provinces
events.evidence: The treaties themselves, the Residency correspondence, and the Chamber of Princes constitution of 1921.
events.note: The game's own title. A sovereignty that exists at somebody else's discretion.

events.title: The indigo system, and the Bengal cultivators who refuse it
events.evidence: The Indigo Commission's evidence, taken from cultivators directly, and Nil Darpan.

events.title: The railway consumes the hardwood forests
events.evidence: Railway procurement figures and forest department returns. Sleeper demand is the reason the Forest Department exists.

events.title: The Archaeological Survey is founded, and the deep past becomes legible
events.evidence: Cunningham's reports, and the excavation record that runs from them to Harappa and Mohenjo-daro in 1921.
events.note: The reason most of this timeline's evidence lines exist. The instrument was colonial; the record is not undone by that.

events.title: Ahmedabad's cotton mills make it the Manchester of the east
events.evidence: The mill company records, the labour returns, and the textile association archive.

events.title: The first Indian Forest Act
events.evidence: The Act itself, and the Forest Department correspondence arguing for it on the strength of railway sleeper demand.
events.note: The state declares forest state property. Customary use becomes a crime in a single clause, and the railways get their sleepers.

events.title: The Orissa famine
events.evidence: The Famine Commission report of 1867, which found the deaths avoidable.

events.title: The Na'anka famine kills a third of coastal Odisha
events.evidence: The Famine Commission report, which found the deaths avoidable, and the export figures for the preceding year.
events.note: Named for the ninth regnal year. A million dead in a province with a surplus the year before.

events.title: A national manuscript survey begins to count what is left
events.evidence: The government manuscript search reports, which are the first attempt to measure the corpus rather than assume it.

events.title: Coffee blight, and then tea
events.evidence: The planters' records, the Hemileia vastatrix outbreak, and the conversion of the estates.

events.title: Shifting cultivation is declared wasteful by people who do not practise it
events.evidence: Forest department reports arguing for suppression of jhum.
events.dispute_text: The colonial forest service treated shifting cultivation as destructive and said so at length. Later agronomy finds long-fallow rotation sustainable at the population densities it was practised at. The reports are evidence of the argument, not of the fact.

events.title: Odia is declared not a language, and proved to be one
events.evidence: The 1870 pamphlet claiming Odia was a Bengali dialect, and the linguistic and literary rebuttal that followed.
events.note: It ended in 1936 with the first Indian province created on a linguistic basis.

events.title: The decennial census begins to sort the population into categories
events.evidence: The census reports themselves, and the caste enumeration schedules and their revisions.
events.note: Categories written down for administrative convenience hardened into identities. That is a mechanic, not a metaphor.

events.title: The Inner Line seals the hills off from the plains by regulation
events.evidence: The Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, and the district administration's correspondence about enforcing it.
events.note: A border drawn to protect a revenue interest, which became the legal shape of the northeast.

events.title: The Buddhist revival and the Panadura debates
events.evidence: The published transcripts of the debates, and Anagarika Dharmapala's Maha Bodhi Society records.

events.title: The Arya Samaj argues for reform by returning to the Vedas
events.evidence: The Satyarth Prakash, and the Samaj's school network.

events.title: The Deccan riots: cultivators burn the moneylenders' bonds, not the moneylenders
events.evidence: The Deccan Riots Commission report and the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act that followed.
events.note: They wanted the paper. The debt was the thing that owned them.

events.title: The Great Famine of the south
events.evidence: Famine Commission reports and grain export figures for the same years.

events.title: Famine kills millions, and then a Famine Code is written
events.evidence: The Famine Commission reports, the mortality estimates, and the export figures for the same years.

events.title: The Forest Act of 1878 divides the forest into three
events.evidence: The Act, which creates reserved, protected and village forest and settles the argument in favour of the first.

events.title: The Marathi press and the public festival as political form
events.evidence: The Kesari and Mahratta files, and the Ganapati and Shivaji festival records from 1893.

events.title: Bankim's Anandamath
events.evidence: The Bengali novel and its serialisation in Bangadarshan.

events.title: U. V. Swaminatha Iyer recovers the Sangam corpus from palm leaf
events.evidence: His own account of the search, and the editions that followed.
events.note: Most of classical Tamil literature was three decades from being unreadable.

events.title: The Sangam texts are recovered from palm leaf and printed
events.evidence: U. V. Swaminatha Iyer's own memoir of the search, and the editions themselves.
events.note: He went house to house asking whether anyone had old palm leaf. Most of Sangam literature is in print because one man did that for fifty years.

events.title: Congress
events.evidence: Inscriptions, copper plates and land grants.

events.title: The Indian National Congress meets for the first time
events.evidence: The proceedings of the Bombay session and its seventy-two delegates.

events.title: The 1885 Kashmir earthquake
events.evidence: The contemporary survey reports and the damage assessments from Srinagar and Baramulla.

events.title: Narayana Guru consecrates a temple, and is asked by what right
events.evidence: The Aruvippuram consecration and the notice he put up: one caste, one religion, one God for man.

events.title: Oil is struck at Digboi
events.evidence: The Assam Railways and Trading Company records and the refinery's own history.

events.title: The Bower manuscript is bought from a treasure-seeker
events.evidence: Hoernle's edition and the account of its purchase in Kucha.

events.title: The movement to unify the Kannada-speaking districts begins
events.evidence: The Karnataka Vidyavardhaka Sangha's records and the district petitions.
events.note: Kannada speakers were split across twenty administrative units. The map the language drew in 850 took eleven hundred years to become a state.

events.title: Sayajirao III makes Baroda's schooling compulsory and its libraries public
events.evidence: The Baroda state education acts, the library department records, and the Oriental Series he funded.
events.note: Free compulsory primary education in an Indian state in 1906, and a public library network to go with it.

events.title: Bose, Ray and Raman: laboratory science in Calcutta
events.evidence: The published papers, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science records, and the 1930 Nobel citation.

events.title: The Assam earthquake
events.evidence: Geological Survey of India investigation, one of the earliest scientific earthquake studies anywhere.

events.title: The Indian famine of 1899
events.evidence: Famine Commission of 1901; the failure of the monsoon that year is instrumentally recorded.

events.title: The Munda ulgulan
events.evidence: Government records, trial documents, and a substantial later ethnographic and oral record.
events.note: A rising against the loss of khuntkatti land rights, led by a man who died in jail at twenty-five.

events.title: The Chhappaniya famine
events.evidence: The famine relief records of the Rajputana states and the mortality returns.
events.note: Named for the Vikram Samvat year 1956. Still the reference point for hardship in the region's speech.

events.title: Stein edits the Rajatarangini and walks the valley to check it
events.evidence: His edition and translation, and the topographical memoir in which he identified Kalhana's place names on the ground.
events.note: He checked a twelfth-century chronicle by walking to every place it named. Most of them were there.

events.title: The Madala Panji temple chronicle is examined as a historical source
events.evidence: The palm-leaf chronicle kept by the Jagannath temple's record-keepers, and the scholarly editions of it.

events.title: Monsoon failure is understood to follow the Pacific
events.evidence: Walker's statistical work on the Southern Oscillation, undertaken by the India Meteorological Department expressly to forecast famine.

events.title: Partition of Bengal
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.

events.title: Bengal is partitioned, and the swadeshi movement answers
events.evidence: The partition order, the boycott records, and the annulment in 1911.

events.title: Indian texts surface at Dunhuang, having survived outside India
events.evidence: The Dunhuang cave library and its dispersal to London, Paris, Beijing and St Petersburg.
events.note: The clearest proof the game's central mechanic is right: what left survived.

events.title: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act concedes what was taken
events.evidence: The Act, which restricts transfer of tribal land — passed eight years after the rising it was answering.

events.title: Gandhi writes Hind Swaraj on a ship
events.evidence: The Gujarati text, written in ten days aboard the Kildonan Castle, and its immediate proscription.

events.title: The campaign for a modern written Telugu splits the literary establishment
events.evidence: The Gidugu Ramamurthy and Vavilala pamphlet war, and the eventual adoption of the spoken register.

events.title: Tagore's Gitanjali, and then his own English of it
events.evidence: The Bengali collection and the 1912 English Song Offerings, which is a different book.

events.title: The Gaekwad Oriental Series begins publishing unpublished manuscripts
events.evidence: The series itself, which printed texts surviving in single copies.

events.title: The Justice Party and the first reservation order
events.evidence: The party's founding manifesto and the Communal Government Order of 1921.

events.title: The Kheda satyagraha: a revenue strike in a failed-harvest year
events.evidence: The revenue department records and the satyagraha's own accounts.

events.title: A critical edition project begins on the Mahabharata
events.evidence: The Bhandarkar Institute's collation of over a thousand manuscripts, which took nearly fifty years.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh
events.evidence: The Hunter Committee evidence, including Dyer's own testimony about what he intended.

events.title: The Rampa rebellion
events.evidence: Government and police records of the campaign in the Godavari agency.

events.title: The Vaikom satyagraha opens the roads around a temple
events.evidence: The satyagraha's records, the Travancore state's concession on three of four roads, and the 1936 Temple Entry Proclamation that followed.

events.title: The Self-Respect movement holds weddings without priests
events.evidence: The Suyamariyathai marriage form, and the 1967 amendment that made it legally valid.

events.title: The Mahad satyagraha drinks from a public tank
events.evidence: The Chavdar tank action, the court case that followed, and the public burning of the Manusmriti in December.

events.title: The Salt March
events.evidence: The march's daily record, the arrest figures, and the salt law it broke.

events.title: The Gilgit manuscripts are found in a stupa
events.evidence: The find itself, among the oldest surviving Buddhist manuscripts anywhere, preserved by being sealed and forgotten.

events.title: the Poona Pact
events.evidence: Texts, and the institutions that outlived the argument.
events.note: Both parties described it afterwards as a defeat. The game should present it that way.

events.title: The Bihar-Nepal earthquake
events.evidence: Instrumental records and the government relief reports.

events.title: The Government of India Act 1935 becomes most of the future constitution
events.evidence: The Act, and the Constituent Assembly's later adoption of large parts of its structure.

events.title: The hill tracts are made Excluded Areas
events.evidence: The Government of India Act 1935.
events.note: Administered separately, which protected some things and removed others, and the argument about which is not over.

events.title: Ambedkar publishes Annihilation of Caste, the speech he was not allowed to give
events.evidence: The printed text, and the correspondence with the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal that cancelled the address.
events.note: Written to be spoken, refused a platform, and printed at the author's own expense. It outlasted the platform.

events.title: The Bengal famine of 1943
events.evidence: The Famine Inquiry Commission report, the shipping and procurement records, and the price series.
events.dispute_text: That the famine happened and that it killed on the order of millions is not in question. Its causation is: crop shortfall, wartime procurement, the denial policy, provincial trade barriers and refusals of imports have all been argued as primary. The game presents the positions.

events.title: Nehru writes The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort
events.evidence: The manuscript, written in prison between April and September 1944.

events.title: Ambedkar and half a million others take Buddhist vows at Nagpur
events.evidence: The announcement of intent at Yeola in 1935 and the conversion at Nagpur, with its twenty-two vows.
events.note: The oldest renouncer tradition in the country, taken up again to answer the oldest question in it.

events.title: The Constitution is drafted, debated and adopted
events.evidence: The Constituent Assembly Debates, twelve volumes of them, and the calligraphed original.
events.note: Three years of argument, recorded verbatim. The last entry in the corpus, and the only one the reader is inside.

events.title: Partition divides libraries and archives
events.evidence: Records of the division of the imperial collections, and the losses in transit and in the violence.

events.title: Independence, and Partition
events.evidence: The Indian Independence Act, the Radcliffe award, and the refugee and mortality records.
events.note: The campaign ends here. Not on a victory screen — on a boundary drawn in five weeks by a man who had never been to India.

events.title: The frontier becomes a schedule in a constitution
events.evidence: The Constituent Assembly debates and the drafting of the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
events.note: Seven thousand years of treeline end as an administrative category, and the campaign ends here without resolving it.

events.title: The Constituent Assembly accepts the abolition of untouchability as a fundamental right
events.evidence: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee report of April 1947 and the Assembly's clause-by-clause debate, including the argument over whether the word should be defined or left to the courts.
events.note: It becomes Article 17 in 1949, two years after the campaign ends. The last thing the game shows you is an argument still in progress.
